title: Sample Complexity of Testing Independence of Counterfactual Categorical Outcomes
banked_reason: The proposed matched, directly evaluable all-regime frontier and attaining full-class test are not delivered: this node explicitly leaves them open and supplies only an unmatched bracket plus lower-bound slices.
gap_reasons: The proposed matched, directly evaluable all-regime frontier and attaining full-class test are not delivered: this node explicitly leaves them open and supplies only an unmatched bracket plus lower-bound slices.
proof_attempt_summary: Two D0 solver rounds and a maximality upgrade produced reviewed count/covariance envelopes, a conservative full-class testing bracket, the matched direct regime, and stronger exact-null collision-degree lower slices. D0.5 correctness and citation checks passed, but the promised explicit matched all-regime frontier and total attaining family remained open behind three load-bearing OEQs, causing a kernel_substituted structural halt confirmed by an independent terminal-validity audit. No formalization or Lean output was attempted; a future retry requires a new observable reciprocal-polynomial certificate with quantitative covariance/nonlinear-null-bias control and a matching normalized arbitrary-mass/growing-alphabet dual, never an identical rerun.
tldr: For a categorical joint outcome after intervention standardization, we prove a finite full-class sample-complexity bracket and an exact-null collision-degree lower-bound hierarchy with unknown masses and interval propensities. At every admissible degree \(L\), the hierarchy excludes all original-record randomized tests through an explicit cutoff of order \(d^{L/(L+1)}\). For fixed small separation and fixed alphabet, degrees \(L\ge2\) eventually strengthen the earlier square-root lower envelope. The direct regime \(d\delta\le1\) is matched at \(k/\delta^2\). The shared-weight certificate, exact normalized sharp dual, and positive matched all-regime frontier remain unresolved.
gap: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy analyze scalar discrete-confounding estimation; Diakonikolas and Kane analyze directly sampled categorical independence. The first supplies unknown-denominator information bounds, and the second supplies outcome-alphabet testing bounds. Neither inspected result resolves an exact intervention-product null with arbitrary conditional dependence and a growing joint alphabet.
fill: Open-ended Question 3 requires the positive matched full-class theorem, including its evaluated frontier and finite attaining family. Open-ended Questions 1 and 2 expose the category-local testing certificate and exact normalized dual that must determine this frontier. The conservative original-count bracket and the supplied-propensity endpoint are mandatory calibration checks.
